projects.title: Pranayama
projects.description: It all began with a breath. With Pranayama, we created a digital space where life's natural rhythm could be felt in every corner of the design. Our challenge was to convey calm, presence and clarity, while guiding visitors towards transformative conscious breathing sessions. From structure to every color, we built a clean site, connected with nature and Kenneth's intention, its creator. The collaboration was as fluid as breath itself, and reminded us that when client and creator flow in harmony, projects breathe on their own.

projects.title: HiPower
projects.description: After calm came expansion. With HiPower, the challenge wasn't just visual, but deeply technical: positioning the brand as a leader in solar energy for industries and businesses. From the start, we knew this site had to be as fast and powerful as the energy source it represents. Between lines of code and SEO strategies, we designed an experience that transmits strength and reliability, without sacrificing beauty. Aerial videos showed the magnitude of their projects, and making everything load in seconds was our trial by fire. This project made us grow as a team: it demanded precision, technical knowledge and a new understanding of what it means to give power... from the web.

projects.title: Terciopelo
projects.description: After connecting with energy, came the moment to transform. With Terciopelo Beauty, Nicky gave us just two words: tarot and esotericism. And with that, we opened the doors to a creative universe where beauty isn't just aesthetic, it's ritual. We designed a site that reflects their rebellious, sensitive and expressive spirit: a salon where every appointment is an act of personal magic. The booking system was key, but what really made this project vibrate was its visual identity, unique and daring, created with artificial intelligence tools to bring every icon and image to life. Terciopelo was our space to play, explore and let the mystical guide the design. Our most creative side found its favorite card here.

projects.title: Bohemian
projects.description: After connecting with energy, came the moment to transform. With The Bohemian, we created an experience that celebrates authenticity and natural beauty. A digital space that breathes creative freedom and connects with those seeking to express their true essence. This project allowed us to explore new frontiers of design, creating a visual identity that fuses organic elements with modern technology, resulting in a platform that invites users to reconnect with their most authentic side.

section1.heading: Web design for authoritative brands: clear, premium, and frictionless
section1.text: Your website shouldn't be a digital brochure. It should guide the user, address objections, and lead to a concrete action: quote, schedule, or buy. That clarity is part of design: making your client understand what you offer, why you're different, and how to request the service without complications.
section1.importaText: Yes, visuals matter. Effects, animations, and micro-interactions are a premium plus when they reinforce your presence and make your brand feel more professional, modern, and established. The difference is that at Aurigital we don't use aesthetics to cover up lack of structure: we build a premium experience with clarity, authority, and structure in the same system.

section2.heading: If you already paid for a website and today you're not proud to show it, the problem isn't your brand
texts: For most of our clients, having a website that looks “pretty” is the number one requirement. And it makes sense. The problem is that “pretty” is subjective: the hard part isn't putting up a “nice” design, but understanding what's beautiful for your brand and executing it with fidelity, criteria, and attention to detail.

At Aurigital, that's part of the job: we listen, interpret, and translate your essence into an experience that represents you. And while you focus on your thing, we take care of what you don't want to and shouldn't have to carry: making the technology excellent and everything work as it should.
section2.bottomText: There are things we solve in every project as standard (clear navigation, flawless mobile experience, order and stability). What really concerns you is this:

faq.titlePart2: about web design in Costa Rica

faqs.question: How do I know if I really need a new website or if adjusting the current one is enough?
faqs.answer: If your current site fails to make people understand what you offer within seconds, doesn't generate measurable inquiries, or works poorly on mobile, it's usually not a "minor adjustment." If the issue is just outdated content or a specific section, adjustments may suffice.

faqs.question: What information do I need to have ready before hiring web design?
faqs.answer: A clear definition of what you sell, who you sell to, main services/products, service area, main site goal (inquiries, sales, scheduling, catalog), and basic brand materials (logo/colors if they exist). If you have visual references, they help align style without improvising.

faqs.question: What should a "high-quality website" deliver beyond looking nice?
faqs.answer: Message clarity, simple navigation, good mobile experience, reasonable load times, working forms, and a structure that guides the user to a concrete action.

faqs.question: What can I realistically expect after publishing my website?
faqs.answer: More trust and credibility, better ability to convert interested visitors into inquiries, and a solid foundation for campaigns or organic growth. It's not realistic to expect automatic sales without a traffic source or a clear offer.

faqs.question: What should be clear in a quote to avoid surprises?
faqs.answer: Scope of sections/pages, what's included and what's not, revision rounds, timelines per stage, whether it includes e-commerce, whether it includes publishing, and how out-of-scope changes will be handled.

faqs.question: Why are some websites very cheap and others more expensive?
faqs.answer: Usually the difference lies in the level of work on structure, prototyping, custom design, revisions, development quality, mobile testing, and post-launch support. Many cheap websites cut corners on those layers and the cost appears later in rebuilding or "patching."

faqs.question: What if I don't have professional photos or ready text?
faqs.answer: You can move forward with provisional material, but perceived quality may drop. Ideally, define what content is essential for launch and what can be improved later without blocking the release.

faqs.question: When does a landing page make sense vs. a full website?
faqs.answer: Landing: when you have a clear offer and want a single action (request/quote). Full site: when the user needs more information to decide (services, trust, proof, questions).

faqs.question: What's the practical difference between "web design" and "web development"?
faqs.answer: Design defines structure, experience, and how the value proposition is communicated. Web development implements functionality, performance, and integrations. They are distinct but complementary stages.

faqs.question: What exactly does "web development" include and what's left out?
faqs.answer: It includes production implementation, base performance, essential security (SSL), agreed integrations, QA, and publishing. Left out is anything not specified: functionalities with private logic, new unplanned integrations, massive content, and scope changes without estimation.

faqs.question: How do you prevent the project from becoming "patches" or becoming unstable over time?
faqs.answer: With clear scope, maintainable technical structure, QA before publishing, and change control. The priority is for the site to remain understandable, stable, and easy to evolve without breaking with each adjustment.

faqs.question: What if during the project I realize I need more features?
faqs.answer: The change is documented, estimated, and prioritized. We prefer to formalize adjustments instead of "adding things" without control, to protect stability, timelines, and quality.

faqs.question: Can I hire development if I already have a design/prototype, or if my site already exists?
faqs.answer: Yes. We can implement from an existing design or work on an already published site, as long as the scope is clear. If the current base limits performance or maintenance, partial or full re-implementation is recommended. Important note: we can work on an existing design but NOT on an already-built website. Most are on site builders like Wix or WordPress. We don't work with or maintain those systems. Even if it's built in code, we can't guarantee the quality of the code we deliver since it wasn't structured by us, and often doing it right means starting from scratch.

faqs.question: How do you handle integrations and automations to reduce manual work?
faqs.answer: We define them based on your real workflow (lead capture, scheduling, orders, communication). We implement agreed integrations (forms, scheduling, payments, CRM/email) and leave the process organized so it doesn't depend on chats for everything.

faqs.question: How "custom" can the development be without becoming a giant system?
faqs.answer: It depends on rules, roles, and flows. If they're specific adjustments, they're integrated within the site. If there's private logic or internal processes (dashboards, portals, ticketing with rules), it's approached as a custom module with its own specification and estimation.

faqs.question: How do you guarantee quality before publishing?
faqs.answer: With an exit checklist: mobile testing, forms, flows, integrations, and final performance and stability review. Ideally we use a staging environment before production to validate without affecting the live site.

faqs.question: What access and ownership do I get at the end of the project?
faqs.answer: You get the access and operational control of the site (accounts, domains/hosting if applicable, and the admin environment). We also leave minimal documentation for continuity and handoff.

faqs.question: What happens after launch if I need changes, support, or evolution?
faqs.answer: You can work on specific improvements by scope, or continue with maintenance/evolution to ensure continuity, updates, and improvements without improvisation. The goal is for the project not to be "abandoned" over time.

items.question: How do I know if I need a full redesign or targeted adjustments?
items.answer: If the problem is structure, message, mobile or conversion, adjusting is usually a patch. On a call we define whether a full redesign or phased redesign makes sense.

items.question: What should I have ready before starting?
items.answer: Offer, audience, main CTA and base assets (logo/identity). If something is missing, we organize it without stalling the project.

items.question: What should a premium website deliver beyond looking good?
items.answer: Clear hierarchy, logical navigation, direct CTAs, flawless mobile, performance and a flow that reduces operational friction.

items.question: What realistic result can I expect when publishing?
items.answer: Better clarity and conversion from day one if the message and flow are right. SEO takes more time; that's why we leave a solid technical foundation.

items.question: Why are some websites so cheap and others more expensive?
items.answer: Quick template vs. custom design with real UX, consistent visual system and solid technical foundation. Cheap usually costs more in friction and reputation.

items.question: What if I don't have professional photos or copy ready?
items.answer: We can start with provisional content and substitute later. The critical part is defining structure, message and CTA.

items.question: When is a landing page better and when is a full site better?
items.answer: Landing if you have one main offer and want direct conversion. Site if you need multiple sections, services, cases, team or blog.

items.question: What is the practical difference between "web design" and "web development"?
items.answer: Design defines experience and UI; development implements it with performance and integrations. At Aurigital, it's solved as a single solution.

items.question: What should be clear in a quote to avoid surprises?
items.answer: Scope, deliverables, revisions, integrations, timelines, what SEO includes and what's left for evolution.

hero.label: Attorneys · Legal Firms
hero.h1: Your law firm deserves a website as solid as your legal reputation
hero.p1: In the practice of law, trust is not asked for — it's built. And it's built long before the first consultation. The web design for lawyers that Aurigital develops starts from that premise: your website is the first argument you present to a potential client, and it must be as rigorous, clear and solid as your legal work.
hero.p2: No templates. No shortcuts. Just a strategic website, custom-designed to reflect the authority and specialization of your firm.

problema.label: The problem
problema.h2: Most websites for lawyers generate distrust without knowing it
problema.intro: A website for lawyers built on a generic template is not neutral — it communicates something. It communicates that the firm has no identity of its own, that its digital presence is a formality and not a strategic investment. For a client evaluating who to trust with a legal matter, that signal matters.

items.h3: A generic design communicates what you don't want to communicate
items.p: Law is a discipline where details determine the outcome. A poorly built website, with inconsistent typography, confusing navigation or predictable stock images, projects exactly the opposite of what a firm needs to project: precision, solidity and judgment. The client who arrives at your website is evaluating whether they can trust you. The design answers that question before they read a single word.

items.h3: The client looking for a lawyer first searches on Google
items.p: Before asking for a referral, before calling, the potential client searches on Google. If your site doesn't appear for relevant searches in your practice area and geographic zone, you don't exist in that decision. And if you appear but the site doesn't generate immediate trust, the client clicks on the next result. Having a website is not enough — you need one that ranks and converts.

solucion.label: The solution
solucion.h2: Website creation for law firms: legal web design built to convert
solucion.intro: The website creation for law firms that Aurigital does doesn't start from an adapted legal template — it starts from your firm, your specialization, your ideal client and the specific objectives you want the site to fulfill. The result is a legal web design that combines visual authority, strategic information architecture and real functionality: a site that works for the firm every day, not just one that exists.

items.h3: Visual authority from the first second
items.p: Every design decision — the palette, typography, visual hierarchy, how practice areas and partner profiles are presented — is made with a clear criterion: generate immediate trust in the visitor. Aurigital designs the site's visual identity so that the first impression is exactly what the firm needs to make: professionalism, solidity and specialization.

items.h3: Information architecture oriented toward capturing consultations
items.p: A client who arrives at a law firm's website has a concrete need and wants to quickly understand if you're the right person to solve it. The information architecture for legal sites that Aurigital designs organizes content to guide the visitor from their problem to the consultation, logically and without friction: clear practice areas, attorney profiles with real credibility and calls to action at the exact moments in the journey.

items.h3: Integrations that professionalize first contact: forms, scheduling and CRM
items.p: The first contact with a potential client sets the tone for the entire relationship. Aurigital integrates scheduling and consultation management systems for lawyers, intelligent forms with automated responses and connection with whatever CRM the firm uses or needs. The site classifies, records and accompanies the potential client from the first message.

proceso.label: The process
proceso.h2: How we build your firm's website
proceso.intro: Every Aurigital project follows a structured process that eliminates surprises and ensures the final result is exactly what the client approved — before a single line of code is written.

items.p: Before entering development, we design the complete site in an interactive navigable prototype. You can browse every section, review how practice areas are presented, validate contact flows and approve the visual design as if the site were already built. Only when you give your approval does development begin. This eliminates late changes, reduces project timelines and ensures there are no gaps between what you expected and what you receive.

items.h3: Development, technical optimization and documented delivery
items.p: With the prototype approved, the Aurigital team builds the site with HTML5, CSS and JavaScript, using the most appropriate technology ecosystem for the project. Responsive design from day one, Core Web Vitals optimization integrated into the code and delivery with complete documentation.

beneficios.label: What's included
beneficios.h2: Everything a serious law firm's website must have

items.h3: Corporate legal web design: brand image that inspires trust
items.p: Corporate legal web design is not just an aesthetic matter — it's a positioning statement. Aurigital builds coherent visual systems that work on the website, in digital communications and at all of the firm's touchpoints: typography, color, hierarchy and tone designed to project exactly the level of professionalism the firm has.

items.h3: Google positioning for local legal searches
items.p: A website that doesn't appear on Google doesn't capture clients. Aurigital integrates technical and semantic SEO from development: URL structure, structured data with schema markup for legal firms, speed optimization and content aligned with the search intent of someone who needs a lawyer in your practice area and geographic zone. The site is built to rank from day one.

items.h3: Responsive design and flawless mobile experience
items.p: The majority of legal service searches in Costa Rica happen from mobile devices. Your firm's website will look and function flawlessly on any device — no design compromises, no broken elements, no forms that don't load. A poor mobile experience not only drives clients away: it directly harms your Google ranking.

items.h3: Plan Paz Mental: your site always operational and updated
items.p: A firm that evolves — new partners, new practice areas, new achievements — needs a website that evolves with it. Aurigital's Plan Paz Mental is a continuous maintenance model from $125 USD/month that includes unlimited content updates, 24/7 technical support, proactive security and performance monitoring, included licenses and a complete redesign at the end of the first two years. No costs per change, no waiting, no intermediaries.

With more than 50 satisfied clients and 11 years of technical experience from its founders, Aurigital is the digital partner chosen by those who built their reputation with rigor and expect the same from every provider.
